reasons: Classification is correct: the grants in 2.1/2.2 run only to Corio, the term "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the Agreement, and there is no notice-based mechanism to add affiliates — that fails the fallback's affiliate element, which the rule treats as material ("must cover our affiliates and contractors").

The finding correctly credits the compliant elements (perpetual/irrevocable, fully paid up, no at-will revocation, M&A assignment right in 14.1 satisfying the transfer element) and confines the redline to the one failing term, so this is not an upgrade of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: inserts "its Affiliates and contractors acting on Corio's behalf" into both grant clauses, extends the internal-use purpose to affiliates, and adds a standard 50% control-based Affiliate definition; no operative counterparty protections were stripped. Changed-character ratios are driven by necessary insertions, not rewriting.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the written-notice fallback.
